result.what: An external link points at a URL that does not resolve.
result.why: Dead outbound links are a quality signal and a bad reader experience, though less costly than internal ones.
result.fix: Update the link, point it at an archived copy, or remove it.

result.what: Page is in the sitemap but no other page on the site links to it.
result.why: Engines weight internal links heavily. An orphan is discoverable only via the sitemap and usually ranks accordingly.
result.fix: Link to it from a relevant page, a hub, or the nav.

liveVerification.method: curl over all 34 sitemap URLs plus targeted checks; no sampling

title.too.long.method: Fetched all 34 sitemap URLs, extracted <title>, HTML-entity-decoded, measured length. Whole set, not a sample.
title.too.long.note: Exactly 60 (/yahoo, /how-it-works) is not over. The 12th page in the crawler count is most likely one of those boundary cases or a raw-entity length count on /mfl or /fantasy-basketball, both of which contain &.

link.broken.external.detail: Both apps.apple.com targets return HTTP 200 when fetched with a browser User-Agent. The crawler's 429 is Apple rate-limiting the crawler, not a dead link. Whole condition tested: href is still on /p/violet-otter-v5cs AND target resolves, so the finding does not hold.

page.orphan.detail: /punishment/new: no page contains href="/punishment/new" exactly. It IS linked from /fantasy-football-punishments and /p/[slug] as "/punishment/new?src=PUNISHMENT_IDEAS" and "?src=PUNISHMENT_RESULT", so the crawler treats the query-string form as a different URL. Real internal-link equity exists; the finding is a query-string artifact. /p/violet-otter-v5cs is a user-generated draw-result page and is orphan by design.
